findings.summary: default_agent removal keys off the string value alone, not the opencode_default_agent_managed provenance flag, so a developer's own default_agent named 'lead' or 'orchestrator' is now deleted -- a regression from main, which explicitly preserved default_agent == 'lead' as a no-op.

findings.location: tests/test_installer.py (no coverage of the update-path deletion branch)
findings.summary: No test exercises default_agent removal for a prior CoDev-set 'lead'/'orchestrator' value on update, and none exercises the developer-owned-value-must-survive boundary finding 1 violates; deleting the whole new if-block leaves all 815 tests green.

The retired agents' frontmatter carried real execution bounds beyond the ADR-0021 permission.task gate the ADR discusses -- edit: deny, a bash allowlist denying raw git commit/push, external_directory: deny, maxTurns, permissionMode: manual. None of these moved anywhere; a skill inherits the ambient session's full permissions. The ADR reasons about the one gate it names and is silent on the rest.

opencode_default_agent_managed is carried forward as True from a pre-0.7.0 lock and never cleared on update, contradicting the code's own comment that CoDev makes no claim over the key going forward. A developer who sets their own default_agent after updating can hit a CoDevError on codev adapter remove, which blocks all deletions.

The mechanical markers that used to verify lead.md/outer-loop-runner.md named the composite verbs (codev slice publish, --selection, codev git mark-ready, etc.) are gone with the files, and nothing scans the new skill for the same invariant -- a future edit dropping one of those verbs from the skill would pass every check.

The 'never pass --body' guard from outer-loop-runner.md's step 6 was dropped when the step became codev slice publish, which structurally has no --body flag, so the live risk is zero -- but ADAPTER_ROLE_PATHS no longer scans skills at all, so this class of guard has no mechanical backstop for any future skill.

default_managed is permanently False now, but still flows through plan_update's OR-with-old-lock logic and _new_lock, and the OpenCodePreparation field name still implies CoDev manages a key it explicitly does not any more. A producer that can only ever emit False is dead code wearing a name that overclaims.

Of the four places the role set is written down, only Justfile's verify-dist and the installer test assert the identical fact (the same sorted .opencode/agents filename list) -- ADAPTER_ROLE_PATHS and OPENCODE_AGENT_CONFIGS hold genuinely different data. The PR description's 'a fourth place' framing overstates the redundancy; only one pair is a true duplicate worth collapsing.

The header says Status: Accepted, but the closing section still reads 'this document's Status line is still Draft. It becomes buildable once that line reads Accepted' -- commit dc5b1ce fixed the header and missed the trailer, leaving the authority document asserting two contradictory things about its own status.

findings.summary: opencode_default_agent_managed provenance flag is never cleared to False when _prepare_opencode deletes default_agent, so CoDev keeps claiming ownership of a key it no longer manages after the deletion runs.

Removing lead as OpenCode's default_agent drops the restrictive permission block (edit: ask, git commit/push: deny, external_directory: deny, task: deny) that constrained the default session; nothing CoDev ships replaces it, and ADR-0044 only reasons about the narrower ADR-0021 specialist-dispatch gate becoming prose-only, not this broader loss.

summary: Plan: lead becomes a skill, not an agent, on every platform
